summary: @hubsync/web-sdk-react preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: The package declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is obfuscated (hex-name identifiers, string-array indirection) and, when invoked by `npm install`, downloads a versioned Bun runtime binary from `github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases`, extracts it to a temp directory, marks it executable, and uses it to run the bundled `math_init.js` file. `math_init.js` is a 727KB `// @bun @bun-cjs`-tagged blob with string-array-rotator obfuscation (`WV8StW` rotator plus a ~2500-entry mixed literal array), whose behavior cannot be read from source. Executing an install-time payload through a freshly-fetched alternate JS runtime is an evasion pattern that bypasses Node-resolved static scanners while giving the shipped payload full code execution on the installer host at install time. The package additionally impersonates an unrelated vendor: `package.json` sets `name: @hubsync/web-sdk-react` but `description: Verdocs Web SDK for React`, and dist bundles reference verdocs.com endpoints, while the @hubsync scope is unrelated to Verdocs — a delivery vector likely to attract developers searching for a Verdocs React SDK.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
